newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says talks with China in Beijing April 9.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says talks with China in Beijing April 9.

text.p: Vietnam and China will hold expert-level talks on their dispute over sovereignty of a South China Sea area in Beijing on April 9, a Foreign Ministry spokesman in Hanoi said on Thursday.

"After China officially agreed with Vietnam's suggestion to hold expert-level talks about the Kan Tan III oil rig, we had suggested that they be held in Hanoi," he told a news conference. "Now China has suggested April 9 in Beijing. For the sake of resolving the issue, Vietnam has agreed."
The spokesman said Hanoi's main goal for the meeting was to clarify that the area in which China's rig was operating was in Vietnam's exclusive economic zone.
He said that the Vietnamese delegation in Beijing would be headed by Nguyen Ba Son, Deputy Director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' International Law Department.
China's drilling in the area, which lies between its southern island province of Hainan and Vietnam's central coast, has sparked verbal sparring between the communist neighbours.

Hanoi has repeatedly demanded that China withdraw the rig and has presented its case to fellow members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. The spokesman said Hanoi advocated solving the issue through bilateral talks but noted that there was strong interest in it from other countries in the region.
